thread:
sam: Pushed profiling run for the multi-GPU Transformer. Seeing a perf regression when we enable LL128 channels — all-reduce time jumps ~2x on the 8xA100 cluster. Repro steps + logs attached.

marta: Ack. Which NCCL envs did you toggle? channels vs default? :thinking_face:

sam: I toggled NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=1 and NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=0 and set NCCL_CHANNELS=8 + NCCL_LL128_ENABLE=1. Baseline (channels=4, LL128 off) had lower all-reduce latency.

ayush: Can you paste the exact env block? want to run the nccl-tests overnight.

sam: Sure. Copy below:
```
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
export NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=1
export NCCL_CHANNELS=8
export NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=0
export NCCL_LL128_ENABLE=1
export NCCL_PROTO=CollNet
export NCCL_ALGO=Ring
```

noah: Hmm NCCL_PROTO=CollNet is for certain topologies. On our DGX-like rack we should try `NCCL_PROTO=LL` or unset it. CollNet can hurt if IB topology != expected. Also try NCCL_ALGO=Tree for small messages.

marta: Good call — also make sure PCI busline P2P is enabled. For KV cache seq lengths we have tiny updates so message size is small -> ring may be fine but channels * message_size impacts fragmentation.

ayush: I'm running nccl-tests/all_reduce with msg sizes {1KB, 4KB, 16KB} across 8 GPUs now. Will post numbers.

deploy-bot: CI profile job #1248 finished: baseline channels=4 LL128=0 all-reduce avg 0.86ms for 4KB, std 0.12ms.

sam: New run with channels=8 LL128=1 gives 1.9ms for 4KB, std 0.3ms. We also saw CPU stalls while waiting on recv. Suggest investigating comm/compute overlap — maybe CUDA streams ordering changed when LL128 enabled.

noah: Are you using CUDA graphs? Graphs + different enqueue order can expose missing stream barriers. Try async-reduces on a separate stream and overlap with compute (use fine-grained events to measure overlap).

marta: Also try lowering NCCL_BUFFSIZE to reduce per-channel buffer fragmentation: NCCL_BUFFSIZE=1048576 -> 524288 may help. LL128 uses larger packets so effective per-channel utilization changes.

ayush: Quick note: nccl-tests with NCCL_BUFFSIZE=512k + LL128 enabled drops 4KB all-reduce to 1.1ms. So tunable.

sam: Nice. Can you add a micro-benchmark that mimics our KV cache update pattern (many 256B updates across heads)? I suspect small-message fanout kills LL128 with 8 channels.

noah: Agreed. Also profile with nvprof/Nsight-cuProf to see if PCIe vs NVLink is hit. If NCCL is using CollNet or NVLink paths incorrectly, we'll see different interconnect bytes.

marta: Let's converge on a config matrix to test overnight: channels {2,4,8}, LL128 {0,1}, BUF {512k,1M}, PROTO {LL,Simple,CollNet}, ALGO {Ring,Tree}. We'll track per-msg latencies and compute overlap.

sam: I'll kick off the matrix on the 8xA100 rack. Will also run our inference harness (seq=2048, batch=1..8) to surface tail latencies.

deploy-bot: Matrix job started: job id 5982. ETA ~6h.

ayush: If we find best config differs by sequence length, we might implement heuristic: for small seq/batch -> channels=2+LL128 off; for large seq -> channels=8+LL128 on. That matches earlier kernel selection heuristics.

sam: Exactly. If heuristics work, we can add a runtime switch and fallbacks (auto-tune at startup) and document in eng-runtime README.

marta: One more thing: check NCCL_VERSION and driver versions. LL128 stability improved in NCCL 2.13+. We should pin and add compatibility tests.

noah: I'll put a short test in eng-releases CI to fail if NCCL<2.13 on our images.

sam: Thanks all. Will post perf table when matrix completes. :white_check_mark:
